title: Ultimate Homemade Pizza Dough
description: The kind that costs about $1.70 per large base but tastes like it should come with its own Italian soundtrack.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, combine cold water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar. Let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Add bread flour, salt, olive oil, and bread improver. Mix until a rough dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 15 minutes until smooth, elastic, and not sticky. The dough should feel soft and spring back when pressed.
Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and rest in a warm spot for 1–1½ hours until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide: full batch for 1 family-sized pizza, half for 2 large pizzas, or quarters for 4 personal pizzas.
Shape each portion into a ball, cover, and let rest for 10–15 minutes to relax the gluten before rolling.
Roll out on a floured surface or stretch by hand to desired thickness. Top and bake at 220–250°C.

notes.title: Flour Matters
notes.content: Bread flour with 12–14% protein gives the best structure and chew. Plain flour will work but will not have the same texture.

notes.title: The Knead
notes.content: Knead for a full 15 minutes — the dough should not be sticky by the end. This develops the gluten properly and gives the crust its characteristic chew. If you have an Ooni spiral mixer, the same timing applies and you will get an even better, more consistent result.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: Dough can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen dough overnight in the refrigerator before using.
